mainTopic: Doubtful קידושין and גירושין, why a שטר קידושין has no date, and the new משנה about two widows tied to two brothers
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבה's reading of the משנה about doubtful קידושין and גירושין, using the case of בר שטיא. אביי says the משנה uses the style of "יגיד עליו ריעו", so each case of doubt applies to both topics. רבא objects from the word "זהו" and gives a one-way rule: every doubt in קידושין is also a doubt in גירושין, but גירושין has extra doubts, such as a problem with the date. The גמרא then asks why the חכמים did not require a date in a שטר קידושין. One answer is that most קידושין are done with money, unlike slaves, who are mostly bought with a document. A second answer is that a dated שטר קידושין could not be kept safe with her, with him, or with the witnesses, and that a גט is different because its date helps her. A new משנה follows about three brothers, a מאמר, and two widows who must do חליצה, with רבי שמעון disagreeing. The גמרא explains that this ruling is only a rabbinic decree and starts a second decree that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The land stayed with בר שטיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רבה with the case of בר שטיא: in a case of doubt, the land was left in its owner's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the land was left in the possession of בר שטיא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רבה's reading of the משנה. It points to the case of בר שטיא, where a doubt was settled by leaving the land with its owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of בר שטיא there was a doubt, and the ruling was to leave things as they were before. The challenge is: here too, a doubtful case should leave the woman in her earlier status. That idea does not fit with רבה's reading of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: they left it standing / kept it
the presumed status, meaning things stay as they were before
a man in an earlier case whose sale of land was in doubt

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a challenge that started before this section. It is not a new statement, so read it as the last punch of the קשיא against רבה.

phrases.english: But the land, they left it
phrases.notes: This points back to the case of בר שטיא that the גמרא brought just before this line.

phrases.english: in the possession of בר שטיא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge to רבה that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reading of the משנה about the cases of doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of בר שטיא, the doubt was settled by keeping the earlier status. So a doubtful case here should also keep the woman's earlier status, and רבה's reading cannot stand.

steps.title: אביי: each case teaches about the other
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבה's reading. He says the משנה uses the style of "יגיד עליו ריעו": a case taught for קידושין also applies to גירושין, and a case taught for גירושין also applies to קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: "His fellow tells about him." The משנה taught a case in קידושין, and the same is true for גירושין. It taught a case in גירושין, and the same is true for קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבה's reading failed, אביי gives a new way to read the משנה. Each case of doubt mentioned for one topic also applies to the other topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists some doubtful cases under קידושין, such as an object landing in between him and her. It lists other doubtful cases under גירושין, such as a doubtful document. אביי says the משנה did not need to repeat each case twice, because each topic "tells about" its partner. So all the cases of doubt are the same for קידושין and גירושין.

keyTerms.meaning: "his fellow tells about him": one case teaches about a similar case
betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: If אביי is right, every doubt is exactly the same in קידושין and גירושין. רבא will now push back on this.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
"His fellow tells about him."
It taught [a case] in betrothal,
phrases.notes: He means the case where it is unclear whether the object landed closer to him or closer to her.

phrases.english: and the same is true for divorce.
It taught [a case] in divorce,
and the same is true for betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's reading after the challenge from בר שטיא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each case of doubt applies only to the topic where the משנה lists it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case listed under one topic also applies to the other topic, so the doubts are the same for both.

steps.title: רבא asks: what does the word "זהו" mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: if the cases are all shared, why does the משנה say "זהו" ("this is"), which sounds like it means only this case?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If it is "his fellow tells about him," what is the meaning of "this is" that the משנה teaches?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's reading by pointing to one word in the משנה, "זהו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says "זהו ספק קידושין" and "זהו ספק גירושין". The word "this is" sounds like it points to these cases and no others. That clashes with אביי's claim that every case of doubt carries over to the other topic.

keyTerms.meaning: "this is": a word that seems to point only to the case named

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If it is "his fellow tells about him,"
what is the "this is" that it teaches?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא אִי יַגִּיד עָלָיו רֵיעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that all cases are shared between קידושין and גירושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "זהו" sounds limiting, as if it means only this case. That does not fit a reading where every case applies to both topics.

steps.title: רבא: גירושין has extra doubts, so "זהו" there is not exact
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own rule. Every doubt in קידושין also exists in גירושין, but גירושין has extra doubts that קידושין does not have. So "זהו" in the גירושין part is not exact. It was written only to match the "זהו" in the קידושין part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Whatever exists in קידושין exists in גירושין, but there are things in גירושין that do not exist in קידושין. And "this is" in the divorce part is not exact. It is only because the משנה taught "this is" in קידושין that it also taught "this is" in גירושין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces אביי's reading with a one-way rule and explains the word "זהו" in the גירושין part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only goes one way: every doubt in קידושין carries over to גירושין, but not every doubt in גירושין carries over to קידושין. So in גירושין, "זהו" cannot be limiting, because the doubts from קידושין also count there. The משנה just used the same word in both places so they would match.

keyTerms.meaning: not exact; not meant to be taken strictly

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is NOT saying the two topics are equal like אביי did. His rule goes only one way, from קידושין to גירושין.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Whatever exists in betrothal exists in divorce,
but there is in divorce what does not exist in betrothal,
and the "this is" of divorce is not exact.
Rather, because it taught "this is" in betrothal,
it also taught "this is" in divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקִידּוּשִׁין יֵשׁ בְּגֵירוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After challenging אביי, רבא offers his own reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: One-way rule, and the word "זהו" is not exact in the גירושין part
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "זהו" in both places limits the doubts to the cases listed there.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין doubts carry over to גירושין, but not the reverse. "זהו" in גירושין is only there to match the קידושין wording.

steps.title: What does "זהו" leave out in קידושין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if "זהו" in the קידושין part IS exact, what case is it meant to leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the "this is" of קידושין, what does it come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question to make רבא's reading complete. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the "זהו" in קידושין is meant exactly, so it must leave something out. The גמרא wants to know which case.

keyTerms.meaning: what does it come to leave out?

phrases.english: And the "this is" of betrothal, to leave out what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question on רבא's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the exact word "זהו" in the קידושין part leaves out

steps.title: It leaves out the date
steps.stepSummary: Answer: "זהו" in קידושין leaves out the issue of the date, which does not matter for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to leave out the date, which does not apply to קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "זהו" in קידושין leaves out a problem with the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A problem with the date can make a גט doubtful. But a document of קידושין does not need a date, so that problem does not create a doubt in קידושין. This is one example of something that exists in גירושין but not in קידושין, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: the date written in a document

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: all doubts are shared between קידושין and גירושין. רבא: every קידושין doubt also applies to גירושין, but גירושין has extra ones, such as a problem with the date. So "זהו" is exact in קידושין and not exact in גירושין.

phrases.english: To leave out the date,
which does not apply to betrothal.
phrases.notes: A betrothal document does not need a date, so a date problem cannot make it doubtful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "זהו" in קידושין leaves out the issue of the date, which does not matter for קידושין.

steps.title: Why is there no required date in a betrothal document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים required a date in a גט but not in a שטר קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the חכמים not require a date in קידושין?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 said the date does not matter in קידושין, so the גמרא now asks why that is. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must have a date by rabbinic rule. The גמרא wants to know why that rule was not also applied to a שטר קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) made a rabbinic rule
Date, here the date written on a document
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: And for what reason did they not institute
a date in betrothal?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא תִּקְּנוּ זְמַן בְּקִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 6's claim that the date does not matter in קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the rabbinic requirement of a date was made for a גט but not for a שטר קידושין.

steps.title: The reason for a date in a גט should also apply to betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The answer is easy if a גט is dated because of פירות. But if it is dated because of the case of בת אחותו, a date should also be required in קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the date in a גט is because of פירות, since an ארוסה has no פירות. But for the one who says it is because of בת אחותו, the חכמים should require a date in קידושין too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that one opinion about why a גט needs a date explains the question easily. The other opinion makes the question into a real challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the date protects the husband's rights to פירות, a betrothal document has no need for a date, because an ארוסה gives him no פירות. If the date exists so a husband cannot quietly protect his niece-wife, who may have sinned, with an undated document, the same trick could be done with an undated שטר קידושין. So that reason should apply to קידושין as well.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (according to one opinion)
Produce or profits from the wife's property
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before נישואין
His sister's daughter, a case where the husband might cover for his wife

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions are about why a גט needs a date. The גמרא is checking which of them also fits קידושין.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
it is because of the profits —
phrases.notes: He means the reason a גט must be dated: so we know when the husband's right to the profits from her property ended.

phrases.english: a betrothed woman has no profits.
But according to the one who says
it is because of his sister's daughter —
phrases.notes: A husband who loves his niece-wife might give her an undated גט to save her if she sinned. The date stops that.

phrases.english: let them institute a date!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the question of step 7 into a challenge against one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that a גט is dated because of בת אחותו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The danger of covering up with an undated document applies to a שטר קידושין too, so the same rule should apply.

steps.title: Betrothal can be done with money, so no date was required
steps.stepSummary: Since קידושין can be done with money or with a document, the חכמים did not require a date in קידושין at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because some people betroth with money and some betroth with a document, the חכמים did not require a date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Many קידושין are done with money, where there is nothing to write a date on, so the חכמים did not make a date rule for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When קידושין is done with money, a date cannot be part of it. Since the חכמים could not apply a date rule to every kind of קידושין, they made no date rule for קידושין at all, not even for קידושין done with a document.

phrases.english: Because there are those who betroth with money
and there are those who betroth with a document,
the Sages did not institute a date.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical limit on making a rabbinic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בת אחותו reason should require a date in a שטר קידושין too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים made no date rule for קידושין, because קידושין is also done with money, where there is no document to date.

steps.title: But a slave's bill of sale does need a date
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף points out that slaves can also be bought with money or a document, yet the חכמים did require a date for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף said to רב אשי: But with a slave, some buy him with money and some with a document, and the חכמים did require a date!
steps.whatsHappening: A challenge to the answer of step 9. Slaves can be acquired in the same two ways, but their document still needs a date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said that having two ways to do something stops the חכמים from requiring a date. The case of a slave seems to show this is not true, since a date is required there.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is a case that shows otherwise

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Yosef, said to Rav Ashi:
But a slave, where there are those who acquire with money
and there are those who acquire with a document,
and the Sages instituted a date!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 9 using a parallel case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that having both a money method and a document method stops the חכמים from requiring a date
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave's sale has the same two methods, yet a date is required, so the reasoning cannot be correct as it stands.

steps.title: It depends on what most people do
steps.stepSummary: Most slaves are bought with a document, so a date was required. Most קידושין are done with money, so no date was required.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, most use a document. Here, most use money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by looking at the usual practice. The חכמים followed whatever method most people use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not only that there are two methods. It is which method is the common one. For slaves the document is the common method, so a date makes sense. For קידושין money is the common method, so the חכמים did not require a date.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority, what most people do

steps.whatToRemember: A גט needs a date, but a שטר קידושין does not. Most קידושין are done with money, and the חכמים based the rule on the common practice. A slave's bill of sale needs a date because most slaves are bought with a document.

phrases.english: There, the majority is with a document,
phrases.notes: "There" means slaves: most people buy them with a document.

phrases.english: here, the majority is with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם רוּבָּא בִּשְׁטָרָא, הָכָא רוּבָּא בְּכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by refining the reasoning of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaves and קידושין are the same, since both can be done with money or a document.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule follows the majority: slaves are mostly bought with a document, so their bill of sale is dated, while קידושין is mostly done with money, so it is not.

steps.title: A second answer: there is no safe place to keep a dated document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new reason why קידושין has no date: it is impossible to arrange it safely. Leaving the document with her or with him both fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say a different reason: it simply cannot work. Where would we keep the document? If we leave it with her, she will erase the date. If we leave it with him, sometimes she is his sister's daughter, and he will cover for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from step 7. It starts checking who could hold a dated שטר קידושין and shows that each option fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date would matter if the woman was unfaithful, to show whether she was already married at that time. If she holds the document, she has a reason to erase the date and protect herself. If he holds it and she is his niece (the בת אחותו case), he may want to protect her and erase it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces a second, alternative answer

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not replace the earlier answer from steps 9-11. It is simply another possible reason why the חכמים did not require a date in קידושין.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
it is because it is not possible.
How would we do it?
Shall we leave it with her?
She will erase it.
Shall we leave it with him?
Sometimes she is his sister's daughter,
and he will cover for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the question of step 7, alongside the answer of steps 9-11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility: no workable way to keep the date safe
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the בת אחותו concern applies to קידושין too, the חכמים should have required a date there.
steps.terutzMaskana: A date in קידושין could not be protected, so requiring it would accomplish nothing.

steps.title: Leaving it with the witnesses does not work either
steps.stepSummary: The third option, giving the document to the witnesses, also fails. Either they remember and need no paper, or they would testify from the paper, which the תורה does not allow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we leave it with the witnesses? If they remember the date, let them come and testify without it. If they do not remember, sometimes they will look at what is written and come testify from that. But the תורה says "from their mouths": not from their writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of options and shows that the last one, the witnesses, fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses remember, the written date adds nothing. If they forget, they might testify only because they read the date, and the תורה requires testimony from the witnesses' own memory (מפיהם). So the written date is either useless or leads to invalid testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: From their mouths, not from their writing: testimony must come from memory

steps.whatToRemember: Second answer: a date in קידושין cannot be kept safely. She would erase it, he might cover for her, and witnesses may not testify from a paper.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם is a basic principle of עדות: witnesses must testify from what they remember, not from what they read.

phrases.english: Shall we leave it with the witnesses?
If they remember,
let them come and testify.
And if not,
sometimes they will see it from the writing
and come and testify,
and the Merciful One said: "From their mouths,"
and not from the mouth of their writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of options begun in step 12 by ruling out the witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witnesses could safely hold the dated document.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses either do not need the date or would testify from writing, which is invalid.

steps.title: Then the same worry should apply to a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second answer: if she might erase the date, the same should be true of a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us say the same about divorce too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second answer. A גט is dated and kept by the woman, so why are the חכמים not worried that she will erase the date there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said a dated document left with the woman is useless because she will erase it. But the חכמים did require a date in a גט, which she also holds. So the worry seems to prove too much.

phrases.english: If so,
let us say the same about divorce too!
phrases.notes: Meaning: she could erase the date on her גט too, so why require one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בְּגֵירוּשִׁין נָמֵי נֵימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 12 by comparing it to a גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that a dated document left with her is useless because she will erase it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט is also dated and kept by her, yet the חכמים required a date, so the fear of erasing cannot be decisive.

steps.title: A גט protects her; a קידושין date works against her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in a גט the date helps her, so she will not erase it. In קידושין the date can only hurt her, so she would erase it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the document comes to save her. Here, it comes to work against her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a difference in her motive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט frees her from being a married woman, so she has every reason to keep it whole and will not tamper with it. A dated שטר קידושין can only prove she was married at a certain time, which might get her punished, so she has a reason to erase it. The second answer therefore stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman will not erase a date that helps her (גט), but she might erase one that works against her (קידושין). That is why only the גט requires a date.

phrases.english: There, it comes to save her;
here, it comes to her disadvantage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 and defends the answer of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases based on the woman's motive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט and a שטר קידושין are the same, since she holds both and could erase either.
steps.terutzMaskana: She protects a גט because it helps her, but she would erase a קידושין date because it can only hurt her.

steps.title: New משנה: three brothers, a מאמר, and two widows
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: one of three brothers dies, the second does מאמר with the widow and then dies too. Both widows must do חליצה with the third brother and may not do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Three brothers were married to three unrelated women. One of them died. The second did מאמר with the widow, and then he died. These women do חליצה and do not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה with a new case. The משנה gives the ruling here, and in the next step it gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the first brother died, the second did מאמר, a rabbinic form of betrothal for a יבמה, but he died before completing יבום. Now two widows, the first brother's widow and the second brother's wife, come before the third brother. The ruling is that both do חליצה and neither may do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks a new משנה
Unrelated women: here it means not related to each other
A rabbinic betrothal done with a יבמה before יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Here נכריות does not mean non-Jewish women. It means the three wives are not related to one another.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three brothers
married to three unrelated women,
and one of them died,
and the second performed מאמר with her,
and he died:
these do חליצה and do not do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁלֹשָׁה אַחִין נְשׂוּאִין שָׁלֹשׁ נׇכְרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion about dating documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the second brother did מאמר with the first brother's widow and then died, both widows do חליצה with the third brother and may not do יבום.

steps.title: The verse behind the ruling: one bond only
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a פסוק to show that יבום applies only to a woman tied to one יבם, not to two.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And one of them dies... her brother-in-law shall come upon her.' This means a woman tied to one יבם, not a woman tied to two יבמין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is still going. It now gives the source for its ruling in Step 16 that both widows get חליצה and not יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first widow is tied in two ways: through her own husband, and through the second brother's מאמר. The משנה reads the פסוק as covering only a woman with one tie, so she is left out of יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
The levirate bond that ties a widow to her husband's brother
The brother-in-law who may do יבום
A double levirate bond, coming from two brothers

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And one of them dies..."
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5. The dots mean the middle of the פסוק is skipped.

phrases.english: "her brother-in-law shall come upon her"
meaning one who has upon her the bond of one yavam,
and not one who has upon her the bond of two yevamin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the ruling in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that both widows need חליצה and cannot have יבום
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 25:5, 'יבמה יבא עליה', read as 'one bond upon her'

steps.title: רבי שמעון: he may marry either one
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees. The third brother may do יבום with whichever widow he wants and חליצה with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: he does יבום with whichever one he wants, and חליצה with the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion. רבי שמעון disagrees with the ruling just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said neither widow can have יבום. רבי שמעון holds that a double bond does not block יבום. He only requires that the brother not take both, so one gets יבום and the other gets חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions in the משנה. The first says both widows get חליצה only. רבי שמעון says one gets יבום (his choice) and the other gets חליצה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
He performs levirate marriage with whichever one he wants,
and performs ḥalitza with the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the ruling in Steps 16–17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third brother may do יבום with either widow and must do חליצה with the other.

steps.title: If it is from the תורה, why is חליצה needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a double bond disqualifies her by the law of the תורה, she should be fully free and need no חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the double bond is a law of the תורה, she should not need חליצה either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It challenges the משנה's ruling that the widows still need חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the law of the תורה, a woman who is outside the מצוה of יבום usually needs no חליצה at all. So if the פסוק really excludes a doubly bound woman, requiring חליצה makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ וְאִי זִיקַת שְׁנֵי יְבָמִין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: GEMARA: And if the double levirate bond is by Torah law,
she should not need ḥalitza either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of the משנה in Steps 16–17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the widows need חליצה, alongside its source from the תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An exclusion from יבום that comes from the תורה should free her from חליצה too, so requiring חליצה contradicts a source in the תורה.

steps.title: It is only a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: The rule is דרבנן, not from the תורה. The חכמים blocked יבום so people would not think a brother may take two widows from one household.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is rabbinic. It is a decree in case people say that two widows coming from one household can both be taken in יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The ban on יבום here is a rabbinic decree, which is why חליצה is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the law of the תורה each widow is the widow of a different brother, so יבום would be allowed. But the second brother did מאמר with the first widow, so it may look as if both women belong to his household. If the third brother married both, people might think one may do יבום with two wives of the same dead brother. That is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree of the חכמים
One household (the wives of one man)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק quoted in the משנה is not the real source of the ban. Since the rule is rabbinic, the פסוק serves only as a support, and that is why חליצה is still required.

phrases.english: Rather, it is by rabbinic law,
and it is a decree lest people say
that two yevamot who come from one household
can both enter levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by moving the rule from Torah law to rabbinic law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the law is דרבנן, not דאורייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double bond blocks יבום by the law of the תורה, which would make חליצה unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is a rabbinic גזירה. By the law of the תורה the widows still need יבום or חליצה, so חליצה is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the סוגיא. Every later question is about how far this rabbinic decree reaches.

steps.title: Why not יבום with one and חליצה with the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the worry is only about taking both, let him do יבום with one widow and חליצה with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him do יבום with one and חליצה with the other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the decree. It suggests a simpler fix that would also avoid the worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree in Step 20 was about marrying two widows from one household. Marrying just one would seem to avoid that problem. This matches רבי שמעון's view, so why did the first opinion forbid יבום for both?

phrases.english: So let him perform levirate marriage with one and ḥalitza with the other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of the decree given in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion's ban on יבום for both widows
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stated worry concerns marrying both, so a split solution would solve it without banning יבום completely.

steps.title: A second decree: a house half built
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with another decree, in case people say that one household can be partly 'built'. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree in case people say: one household, part of it built...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to why the split solution is not allowed. The full answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing יבום with one widow and חליצה with the other might make people think one household can be partly 'built' and partly not. The idea of 'building' a brother's house is how the תורה describes יבום. The concern is fully spelled out in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: Built; here, a household continued through יבום

phrases.english: It is a decree lest people say:
one household, part of it is built

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ: בַּיִת אֶחָד, מִקְצָתוֹ בָּנוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 with an additional rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Doing יבום with one widow and חליצה with the other would avoid the problem of marrying two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting is also blocked, in case people come to think one household can be partly 'built'. The rest of the explanation continues on the next amud.
